title: Electro-oxidative treatment of municipal sludge: a sustainable approach for bacterial control
content: This study evaluated electrooxidation (EO) using mixed metal oxide (MMO) anodes for stabilizing and disinfecting waste-activated sludge. Batch experiments took place at current densities of 7.14 to 11.90 mA cm−2 with 1.25 g per L NaCl for 10 minutes. Under optimized conditions, EO achieved over 99.9% bacterial inactivation along with significant reductions in organic load, including about 45% COD, 51% BOD, and 27% TOC removal. Nutrient transformation occurred, with about 96% phosphorus reduction and increased soluble nitrogen species due to mineralization. EO treatment also lowered odorous gas emissions; H2S and NH3 concentrations decreased from 10.18 to 2.99 mg L−1 and from 9.04 to 1.55 mg L−1, respectively. The MMO anodes showed high stability with minimal compositional changes after 50 cycles. The treated sludge remained suitable for vermicomposting, confirming its compatibility with downstream biological processes. These findings indicate that EO offers a fast and effective pretreatment strategy for improving sludge stability, biosafety, and resource recovery potential.
